classical-hollywood.name: Classical Hollywood
classical-hollywood.description: Studio-era filmmaking built on continuity editing, stars and genre, within which a few directors developed strong personal styles.

german-expressionism.name: German Expressionism
german-expressionism.description: Distorted sets, heavy shadow and subjective camera used to externalise inner states.

soviet-montage.name: Soviet Montage
soviet-montage.description: Editing treated as the essence of cinema: meaning comes from the collision of shots.

poetic-realism.name: Poetic Realism
poetic-realism.description: Fatalistic French stories of ordinary lives, shot with studio lyricism.

italian-neorealism.name: Italian Neorealism
italian-neorealism.description: Location shooting, non-professional actors and stories of ordinary people in postwar Italy.

art-cinema.name: Postwar modernist art cinema
art-cinema.description: Auteur-driven films that loosen plot and foreground ambiguity, subjectivity and form.

french-new-wave.name: French New Wave
french-new-wave.description: Critics turned directors who shot cheaply on location and broke the rules of continuity and tone.

left-bank.name: Left Bank group
left-bank.description: The literary, politically engaged wing of the French New Wave, preoccupied with memory and documentary.

japanese-golden-age.name: Japanese studio golden age
japanese-golden-age.description: The studio-era masters whose films reached the West in the 1950s.

japanese-new-wave.name: Japanese New Wave
japanese-new-wave.description: A generation that attacked the humanism of the studio masters with sex, politics and formal rupture.

czechoslovak-new-wave.name: Czechoslovak New Wave
czechoslovak-new-wave.description: Satire, non-actors and formal play under, and against, state socialism.

new-hollywood.name: New Hollywood
new-hollywood.description: A film-literate generation that brought European art-cinema methods into American genre film.

new-german-cinema.name: New German Cinema
new-german-cinema.description: Young West German directors confronting the national past with low budgets and personal styles.

american-independent.name: American independent cinema
american-independent.description: Directors working outside or at the edge of the studio system. A production context more than a shared style.

taiwan-new-wave.name: Taiwan New Wave
taiwan-new-wave.description: Long takes, distant framing and everyday life used to examine Taiwan's history and modernisation.

hong-kong-second-wave.name: Hong Kong Second Wave
hong-kong-second-wave.description: Auteur filmmaking that grew out of Hong Kong's commercial industry, restless in style and preoccupied with time and identity.

korean-new-wave.name: Korean New Wave
korean-new-wave.description: High-craft genre films that fold in social critique and abrupt shifts of tone.

iranian-new-wave.name: Iranian New Wave
iranian-new-wave.description: Poetic realism that blurs fiction and documentary, often through children and non-actors.

dogme-95.name: Dogme 95
dogme-95.description: A manifesto of handheld cameras, natural light and location sound, against technical polish.

surrealism.name: Surrealism
surrealism.description: Dream imagery and irrational juxtaposition aimed against bourgeois logic.

spaghetti-western.name: Spaghetti Western
spaghetti-western.description: Italian-made westerns that turned the genre operatic, cynical and violent.

parallel-cinema.name: Parallel Cinema
parallel-cinema.description: A realist alternative to mainstream Indian cinema, rooted in Bengali literature and neorealism.

slow-cinema.name: Slow cinema
slow-cinema.description: Very long takes, minimal narrative and attention to duration and stillness.

transcendental-style.name: Transcendental style
transcendental-style.description: An austere style that withholds expression and drama to point beyond the everyday.

social-realism.name: Social realism
social-realism.description: Working-class lives filmed with documentary methods and little stylisation.

postmodern.name: Postmodern cinema
postmodern.description: Pastiche, quotation and genre mixing, with irony about the film's own artifice.

silent-comedy.name: Silent comedy
silent-comedy.description: Physical comedy built from long, wide takes that prove the gag was really performed.

romanian-new-wave.name: Romanian New Wave
romanian-new-wave.description: Long handheld takes, real-time pacing and dark humour about life during and after Ceausescu.

fifth-generation.name: Chinese Fifth Generation
fifth-generation.description: The first class to graduate after the Cultural Revolution, turning to landscape, colour and history in place of socialist realism.

sixth-generation.name: Chinese Sixth Generation
sixth-generation.description: Low-budget, often unofficial films about contemporary urban and provincial China, shot in a documentary manner.

cinema-novo.name: Cinema Novo
cinema-novo.description: Brazilian political cinema made cheaply and roughly by design, mixing neorealism, folklore and agitation.

greek-weird-wave.name: Greek Weird Wave
greek-weird-wave.description: Deadpan, absurd allegories of family and power, delivered in stilted speech.

film-noir.name: Film noir
film-noir.description: Shadowy American crime films about fate, corruption and desire, shaped by German émigrés and hard-boiled fiction.

hollywood-musical.name: Hollywood musical
hollywood-musical.description: Studio films organised around song and dance numbers, at their height in MGM's Freed unit.

screwball-comedy.name: Screwball and sophisticated comedy
screwball-comedy.description: Fast, verbal Hollywood comedies of class, courtship and remarriage.

silent-pioneers.name: Silent-era pioneers
silent-pioneers.description: The directors who established feature-length storytelling, the epic and the star system before sound.

soviet-thaw.name: Soviet cinema after the Thaw
soviet-thaw.description: Soviet filmmakers who used the loosening after Stalin to pursue personal, poetic and often censored work.

french-classical.name: French classical cinema
french-classical.description: French studio-era craftsmanship outside the New Wave: polished scripts, genre films and poetic fantasy.

post-new-wave.name: French post-New Wave
post-new-wave.description: The generation after the New Wave, harsher or more extravagant than its predecessors.

documentary.name: Documentary traditions
documentary.description: Non-fiction filmmaking, from staged ethnography to direct cinema, testimony and the essay.

experimental.name: Avant-garde and experimental film
experimental.description: Artists' films made outside the industry that explore perception, duration and the medium itself.

british-studio-era.name: British studio era
british-studio-era.description: The peak of British studio filmmaking, from Ealing comedy to the Archers and David Lean.

british-new-wave.name: British New Wave
british-new-wave.description: Working-class stories and location shooting, growing out of the Free Cinema documentaries.

british-art-cinema.name: British art cinema
british-art-cinema.description: British directors working in a personal, formally adventurous mode outside the realist mainstream.

contemporary-hollywood.name: Contemporary Hollywood
contemporary-hollywood.description: The era of the blockbuster and the franchise, in which a few directors keep a recognisable signature at very large scale.

horror.name: Horror
horror.description: The genre of fear, from Universal's monsters to independent American horror and the Italian giallo.

animation.name: Animation
animation.description: Feature animation, from Disney's studio system to Studio Ghibli.

third-cinema.name: Third Cinema and African cinema
third-cinema.description: Militant, anti-colonial filmmaking from Latin America and Africa, defined against both Hollywood and European art cinema.

italian-political-cinema.name: Italian political cinema
italian-political-cinema.description: Investigative films about power, crime and colonial war, growing out of neorealism.

spanish-cinema.name: Spanish cinema under Franco
spanish-cinema.description: Films that spoke about Spain through satire, allegory and childhood because they could not speak directly.

polish-film-school.name: Polish Film School
polish-film-school.description: The first postwar generation of Polish directors, reckoning with the war and its myths.

la-rebellion.name: L.A. Rebellion
la-rebellion.description: Black filmmakers trained at UCLA who rejected Hollywood models for independent, community-rooted work.

new-queer-cinema.name: New Queer Cinema
new-queer-cinema.description: Independent films that treated queer lives with formal daring and without apology.

hollywood-comedy.name: Hollywood comedy since 1960
hollywood-comedy.description: Studio comedy after the classical era: parody, improvisation and the teen film.

australian-new-wave.name: Australian New Wave
australian-new-wave.description: A state-supported revival that produced both atmospheric art films and genre hits.
